notes.text: Almost all Belgian mortgages are fixed-rate annuities with a constant nominal payment over the life of the loan, and ECB data show only about 7% of new house-purchase lending in 2025 and August 2026 was floating or fixed for up to one year. Combined with automatic wage indexation, which lifted average nominal disposable income by 29% between early 2019 and early 2025, this sharply reduced debt-service burdens on pre-2022 loans and explains why the market saw a soft landing rather than a correction when rates rose.

notes.text: Since 2020 the National Bank of Belgium's supervisory expectations have limited high loan-to-value lending, differentiated for first-time buyers, other owner-occupiers and buy-to-let; for example, up to 35% of first-time buyer loans may exceed 90% LTV and only 10% of buy-to-let loans may exceed 80%, and banks have over-complied. Citing lower risk, the NBB is folding its 6% sectoral mortgage buffer into a countercyclical buffer raised from 1.0% to 1.25% from 1 July 2026.

notes.text: Flanders and Wallonia cut registration taxes on home purchases at the start of 2025, which the NBB credits with reviving nominal price growth to 1.6% in 2025 Q1 on its hedonic index after three years of broadly flat nominal prices and a real decline of more than 10% from the 2021 peak. Because the cuts were made by the regions, tax-driven price effects can differ across the country.
